# Mixed-direction line layout

Original independent OOXML control generated by `tools/bidi_layout_fixture.py`.
The generator reuses only the OPC skeleton of our original rtl-runs fixture;
no third-party document is incorporated. The reference application exported
`native.pdf` using `tools/export-reference.ps1`.
`tools/record_bidi_layout_reference.py` extracts baselines, glyph origins and
font names through PDFium. `reference.json` binds source/PDF/case hashes.

Eighteen cases on three Letter pages use Arial 10pt in all font slots. Cases
1–14 pair ordinary and forced-RTL Latin, European digits, Arabic-Indic digits,
Hebrew, Arabic, mixed bracketed text and a single Arabic-Indic zero. Cases
15–16 constrain mixed text to 110pt; case 17 includes two tabs; case 18 joins
Arabic lam/alef. Body lines are exactly 24pt, labels 12pt.

The browser test feeds equivalent original internal paragraphs to shared
layout/measurement/paint. It verifies page/line counts, baselines within .25pt,
the last suffix glyph within .3pt, and resolved Hebrew/Latin/number order.
All three native/app page pairs were visually inspected, including Arabic
joining and mirrored brackets. PDF ToUnicode is not a reliable bracket or
ligature-order oracle, so those are not inferred from extracted strings.

Cases 15–16 caught an incorrect treatment of explicit RTL spaces as ordinary
hanging LTR line tails. Part 1 §17.3.2.30 supplies higher-level directionality
for neutrals; the reference application retains those resolved R spaces at the visual start of the
RTL group. Their advance must participate in line fitting. This is not a new
reference/spec divergence. Strong LTR text with rtl true, or strong RTL text with
rtl false, remains specification-unspecified and is native compatibility data.

This is component coverage, not editable RTL DOCX support. Active flags remain
guarded. Pointer and vertical affinity now have independent regressions.
Logical character navigation is validated below; optional visual navigation is
not implemented. Open work includes full weak/neutral classification and
explicit Unicode controls, paragraph bidi/embedding markup, directional
small-caps parts, decoration/clipping edge cases and contextual font choice.
The adapter uses MIT bidi-js 1.0.3 (Unicode 13 data) for embedding levels and
classification; original code handles UTF-16/grapheme mapping and L1/L2 line
ordering. It does not imply support for newer Unicode bidi data.

## Native caret positions

`tools/record-bidi-carets.ps1` opens a private read-only reference application instance, confirms
the exact source, repaginates, and records collapsed main-story ranges in
`native-carets.json`. It closes only its own document/application and binds the
results to the source hash. The automation API documentation describes the coordinate units and the
unavailable sentinel for [WdInformation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/office/vba/api/word.wdinformation);
the recorder rejects negative positions. This host's reference application at 100%
zoom rounds the returned positions to .75pt screen pixels.

The browser test verifies 23 interior Hebrew/Arabic positions within .5pt of
the reference application (observed maximum .4275pt), their hit tests and a lam-alef selection.
Whole-fragment DOM ranges supply contextual caret advances from the browser's
shaper; Canvas still measures and paints glyphs. Each finished RTL fragment
requests geometry once, rather than during prefix measurement. Source offsets
map to shaped-text indices, including omitted soft hyphens. Horizontal text
transforms also scale caret advances. Hidden measurement nodes are removed.

## Native character commands

`tools/record-bidi-navigation.ps1` records `WordBasic.CharLeft`/`CharRight` in
both values of [Options.CursorMovement](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/office/vba/api/word.options.cursormovement).
The automation API documentation describes logical and visual modes as distinct choices. The recorder
uses its own read-only document/application and restores and checks the original
cursor preference before closing. It does not send physical keyboard input.

`native-navigation.json` binds 128 recorded states to the source hash. Four cases
cover Hebrew, Arabic, narrow wrapping and lam-alef; each records eight states
per direction in each mode. The browser checks the 64 logical-mode states,
including identical source offsets and caret coordinates within .5pt of the reference application's
screen-rounded range information. Logical mode was the host's original setting.
Visual-mode data is retained as separate evidence, not as the editor's policy
or a claim that range information resolves every visual boundary affinity.

The existing logical movement passes; replacing it merely because RTL text is
present would change interaction policy. This evidence closes the presumed
logical horizontal-movement gap without enabling full RTL DOCX editing. Run
formatting, remaining script/shaping cases and round-trip editing still require
validation and implementation.
The three rendered pages remain RGB-identical to the preceding capture.

This proves interior caret placement for these controls, not native keyboard
navigation or ambiguous run-boundary affinity. Small-caps/multiple-font parts
still use the prior fallback and remain outside activation, as do per-character
Arabic color/decorations whose shaping boundaries need separate verification.
